senses.gloss:
Aulāna is a word occurring in a single passage of the
Rigveda,^1 where it may possibly be a patronymic of Śaṃtanu
as a ‘descendant of Ula.’ Ludwig,^2 however, conjectures that
the reading should be ‘Kaulāna.’ Sieg^3 regards Aulāna as
a later descendant^4 of Śaṃtanu, who utilized the story of
Devāpi's rain-making as an introduction to his rain hymn.
1) x. 98, 11.
2) Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 166.
3) Die Sagenstoffe des Ṛgveda, 141.
4) Cf. Sāyaṇa on Rv. x, 98, 11; Kuru
kula-jātaḥ Śāṃtaṇavaḥ, ‘a descendant
of Śaṃtanu, born in the family of the
Kurus
